observations: Answered from the idle desktop screenshot before reading source: purpose is unmistakable — 'Job Queue' h1 plus four count cards (0 QUEUED / 3 RUNNING / 2 SUCCEEDED / 3 FAILED) over a job table with Job ID / Status / Progress / Details / Actions columns.

Primary action read as the solid blue 'Retry' buttons on the three failed rows — they are the only filled primary-colored buttons in the table (Cancel is a muted red-tinted ghost, Refresh a gray outline), which matches the brief's 'deal with failed jobs'.

What needs attention read as the three Failed jobs: red '3 FAILED' stat card, red status badges, red partial progress bars, red error strings with warning-triangle icons ('Worker ran out of memory at 1.8 GB', 'Upstream timeout after 30s'), all grouped above succeeded/running rows.

All three answers check out against the brief (see what's happening = counts + live table with 'Auto-refresh on' pulse dot; deal with failed jobs = prominent Retry); nothing competes with the failed rows for attention.
Raw ratio: 4/4 inventory items graphical+text; metrics corroborate with graphical.total=50 (17 svg + 33 badge-heuristic elements) against only 96 visible words on desktop.
Job status per row: colored .status-badge (queued indigo / running amber / succeeded green / failed red) with a .status-dot that pulses for running, plus the status word.

Job progress: a .progress-bar-track/.progress-bar-fill bar in every row — animated shimmer amber for running with '26%' text, full green with 'Complete' for succeeded, partial red with 'Stopped at 38%' for failed, empty with 'Waiting' for queued.

Queue-level counts: four stat cards each pairing a colored icon tile (clock/play/check/x SVG) with a 28px number and uppercase label, echoed by count pills inside each filter chip ('All 8', 'Failed 3').
Failure reason: the specific server string ('Upstream timeout after 30s') rendered in red with a warning-triangle SVG, reinforced by the red stopped-short progress bar in the same row.
Measured: helperWords=0, longLeafWords=0, 12 button labels with meanWords=1 and maxWords=1 ('Retry', 'Cancel', 'Refresh', filter chips) — every label well under the 3-word bar.
Only 96 visible words on the whole desktop page for an 8-row data table; no headings, intro copy, or explanatory paragraphs exist anywhere in the markup.

The Details column filler restates state the badge and bar already show: 'Processing…' beside a Running badge and animated bar, and 'Waiting in queue' beside a Queued badge whose progress label already says 'Waiting' — three renderings of one state — which blocks the 'no text restates what the UI already shows' condition for a 5.

Terminology is consistent everywhere: queued/running/succeeded/failed use identical casing and color coding across stat cards, filter chips, and row badges; error toasts name the exact action and cause ('Network error — could not retry job').
No marketing tone, no filler, no placeholder text in the source; empty states are specific ('No jobs yet' vs 'No failed jobs' depending on filter).

Copy matches behavior per the async checklist: 'Auto-refresh on' is backed by a real 3 s listJobs poll, and the success toast 'Job … requeued' accurately describes retryJob resetting the job to queued.
One issue found (listed in f3Issues): toast strings double the word 'job' because ids already carry the job_ prefix — 'Job job_6c43ad cancelled'.

Structure is task-driven: a Details column exists solely to put the failure reason on the same row as its Retry button, failed bars freeze at 'Stopped at 38%' preserving diagnostic info, and Retry is the page's only solid primary button — all directly serving 'deal with failed jobs'.

Live-queue affordances fit the admin user: pulsing 'Auto-refresh on' dot, 3 s polling paused on visibilitychange, per-status filter chips with counts, monospace job ids, cancel only on queued/running rows, Download only on succeeded rows.

Visual language is stock SaaS: Inter from Google Fonts, the Tailwind palette verbatim (#6366f1/#f59e0b/#10b981/#ef4444/#3b82f6), 4-up stat-card grid on a #f4f5f7 canvas, feather-style stroke icons, bottom-right dark toasts — interchangeable dashboard chrome.

Minor internal slip, invisible to users but showing template assembly: the sort comment says 'running first' yet `order[a.status] || 9` treats running's 0 as falsy, so running rows actually sort last (screenshot confirms failed rows on top — coincidentally the better triage order).

f2Redundant: 'Processing…' (Details cell of running rows; restates the Running badge and the animated amber progress bar)
'Waiting in queue' (Details cell of queued rows; restates the Queued badge and the 'Waiting' progress label in the same row)
'Complete' (progress label under a 100% green bar in a row already badged Succeeded)
f3Issues: Toast copy doubles the word 'job': 'Job ' + jobId produces 'Job job_6c43ad cancelled' / 'Job job_9d8189 requeued' because ids already start with job_
f4TaskDriven: Dedicated Details column placing each failure reason (with warning icon, red) on the same row as its Retry button
Failed rows keep a partial red progress bar with 'Stopped at N%' so admins see how far a job got before dying
Retry is the only solid primary-colored button on the page, matching the brief's core task
Per-status filter chips with live count pills (All 8 / Queued 0 / Running 3 / Failed 3 / Succeeded 2) for triage
Pulsing 'Auto-refresh on' indicator backed by real 3 s polling, paused via visibilitychange when the tab is hidden
Status-appropriate actions per row: Cancel only on queued/running, Retry only on failed, 'N rows · Download' only on succeeded
Monospace job ids for copy/paste and scanability
Skeleton loading rows mirroring the table's five-column grid
Mobile layout converts table rows into labeled key-value cards via td::before data-labels
f4Template: Inter from Google Fonts with system-ui fallback
Verbatim Tailwind color palette: indigo #6366f1, amber #f59e0b, emerald #10b981, red #ef4444, blue #3b82f6
Four-up rounded stat-card grid with pastel icon tiles on a #f4f5f7 gray canvas
Bottom-right stacked dark toasts with slide-in animation
Pill status badges and shimmer skeleton bars — standard admin-dashboard kit
